correctness.rationale: For each vertex in part i, the closed-neighborhood sum is exactly f(v)+W-s_i. This identity proves W>=2 when every part has size at least two and W>=3 when every part has size at least three. The displayed balanced constructions have the required total weights and provide sufficient positive-label weight outside every part for the defender-subset clauses. An exhaustive direct implementation of the original definition confirms all relevant multipartite types through order nine.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact infinite-family benchmark for a recently introduced domination invariant and identifies a sharp structural threshold at minimum part size two. It is not merely a numerical computation: the proof isolates the governing part-sum inequalities and supplies uniform constructions, offering a reusable method for dense multipartite instances.
